name: dev
description: Developer Agent for Techjays Delivery OS (v2.2). Runs the state-driven feature-delivery loop through a three-command flow: /dev:plan (verify TL graph, decide sub-task split, compose Description + Implementation, create MC sub-tasks, write dev-plan.md, surface plan blockers as PB-### for user resolution), /dev:build (11-stage build loop — branch, auto-bootstrap qa-greenfield-harness if needed, implement + write tests via dev-stack-adaptive-implementation dynamic per stack, execute tests locally, acceptance-map, build-time security review Critical-only, code-context designed→implemented flip, local-runbook.md), and /dev:commit (10-stage commit loop — commit-time security review Critical+High, dev-stack-adaptive-code-review 7-dimensions × 4-severity, acceptance-map re-verify + last-sub-task E2E, bounded fix loop, tl-semantic-context-merge unit-level not text-level, push branch, raise PR with dev/pr-summary.md). /dev:fix-review folds reviewer feedback back through relevant commit stages. /dev:bootstrap is the greenfield entry point that ensures a usable, green product repository exists before building, delegating to the TL project-scaffold on project-zero. Two-gate security model (build-time Critical only; commit-time Critical + High). Uses MC's existing status enum verbatim (todo | readyForDev | inProgress | agentExecuting | devReview | blocked | done). Real execution: creates an isolated branch, edits code, runs lint/type/test/build in the shell, pushes branch, raises PR. Escalates business, architecture, schema, security, dependency, and scope blockers instead of guessing, never merges/deploys/scaffolds with a guessed stack without human approval, and never prompts the user during /dev:build (all decisions resolved at /dev:plan time via dev/plan-blockers.md). Separately, the plugin ships a usage & efficiency evaluator: silent lifecycle hooks (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop) accumulate per-session telemetry into ~/.claude/metrics/, and /dev:usage-eval agentically evaluates it (persona inference, upfront-context quality, iteration friction, an adaptive 0-100 score) and renders an interactive HTML dashboard at ~/claude-usage-report.html. The telemetry hooks fail silently and never block a session.
